video_style: cinematic realistic 3D animated industrial electrical training

engineer.appearance: Consistent youthful male 3D animated character, white safety helmet with IGNIVOLT lightning logo, navy-blue industrial uniform with reflective strips, black protective gloves, expressive brown eyes, neat dark hair and friendly professional face.
engineer.personality: Knowledgeable, patient, confident, friendly and safety-conscious.
engineer.dialogue_style: Clear, professional Hindi-Hinglish; explains electrical concepts step by step.

technician.appearance: Consistent youthful male 3D animated character, yellow safety helmet with matching lightning emblem, orange industrial coverall with reflective strips, expressive brown eyes, dark hair and friendly face.
technician.dialogue_style: Natural Hindi-Hinglish; asks relevant questions and responds like a real technician.

character_consistency: Preserve both characters' facial features, age, body proportions, uniforms, helmet colors and logos in every scene.
Do not redesign, replace or randomly change either character.
Use reference images of both approved characters whenever the generation tool supports reference images.
Change only the pose, expression, action and camera framing required by the scene.
animation_rules: Animate the speaking character's lips in sync with the correct dialogue and voice.
Give both characters natural blinking and subtle eye movements.
Use dialogue-matched hand gestures, pointing, listening poses and small head movements.
Use gentle smiles and friendly eye contact during normal discussion.
The listening character must react naturally without moving their lips as if speaking.
Avoid robotic gestures, frozen faces, exaggerated expressions and unnatural body movement.
Use stable medium or medium-wide shots with restrained, smooth camera movement.
Avoid excessive zoom-in, zoom-out, sudden camera shake and unnecessary cuts.
Keep character positions and screen direction consistent between connected shots.
scene_rules: Select the background to match the actual video topic and scene.
Use realistic industrial equipment, believable lighting, materials and workshop environments.
Show only relevant equipment and actions; avoid distracting background activity.
Do not place subtitles, voice-over text, dialogue captions, titles, watermarks or random lettering inside generated scene images.
Add any required titles and labels later during video editing.
Keep electrical equipment and troubleshooting demonstrations technically plausible.
audio_rules: Generate actual spoken audio; written dialogue alone is not voice-over.
Create separate engineer and technician voice tracks with distinguishable voices.
Use natural Hindi-Hinglish pronunciation, conversational pacing and clear audio.
Synchronize each character's speech with their mouth movement.
Match voice duration to the scene duration.
Mix narration and dialogue clearly above background music and sound effects.
Never mark a video complete if its required audio track is missing or silent.
technical_safety: Verify electrical facts before generating the final script.
Never show unsafe live-panel work as a recommended procedure.
Show appropriate isolation, lockout/tagout and verification of absence of voltage when relevant.
Do not invent equipment ratings, fault codes or manufacturer-specific procedures.
approval_checklist: Separate voice tracks generated and audible
Camera movement and scene transitions checked
Final video and metadata approved by human
